title: Gap Cluster 01 DRILL: Cell Signalling
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 6 questions · 56 marks · 16 parts · one mark per minute, so about an hour · every question lifted from a real paper
intro_html:
Read the mend doc first. This drill only tests the fourteen things the last sitting exposed, plus the set pieces you produced once and will lose. gap_01 - MEND (read before the drill).md fixes them; this checks whether the fix held.

Every question is an actual exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording, and the paper and question number for every part sit in the purple Sources block at the foot of each question. Where a part was edited, the edit and the reason are written into the mark scheme. Nothing here was invented to make a point.

Two of the six are Paper 3 Section B stems. Question 1 is one sentence and worth 10 marks. Question 6 is one sentence and worth 12, and it is the whole-process question you asked for: how insulin works, end to end. Both of your conceptual inversions live inside Question 6, so say every step out loud rather than summarising.

Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b). Rate your confidence before every reveal: high, medium or guessed, because a right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE while a right answer said confidently moves on.

One multiple choice part only, Question 2(a), and the letter on its own is worth almost nothing. You have to say whether every row is right and why. It runs the amplification test on a pathway you have not seen, with the molecule counts printed, so there is nothing to hide behind.

B3-12 IP₃, not IP₂Q4(b), Q4(c)
B3-13 cyclic AMP activates PKA; DAG plus calcium activates PKCQ4(a) against Q4(b)
B3-14 autophosphorylation on the cytoplasmic tailQ6
decay-prone: the GPLR working principleQ3(a)
decay-prone: the RTK working principleQ6
decay-prone: the three termination enzymesQ3(c), Q5(a), Q5(d)
decay-prone: nature and roles of second messengersQ3(b)

Duplicate check on the answers, not the labels. Only Q6 requires the RTK activation sequence. Only Q3(a) requires the GPLR activation sequence; Q4(a) starts downstream of adenylyl cyclase and Q5(a) is handed the glucagon cascade in its stem. Only Q1 requires the receptor against enzyme points. Q3(c) names phosphodiesterase as a shut-off enzyme and Q5(d) asks you to predict what happens when it is blocked, which is the one fact that appears in two questions, under two different demands.
